name: IRHYTHM HOLDINGS INC

priced.reason: not a repriceable fcff name or no growth supplied

devils_advocate.strongest_counter: That no_model here is intellectual cowardice on a name where the picture is actually clear. iRhythm has $591.3 million of cash and securities, is guiding to $880-890 million of revenue at a 13-14% adjusted EBITDA margin, generated $51.1 million of operating cash flow in Q2 alone, and trades at 4.2x forward sales against a health-care cohort median EV/sales of 4.8x. That is enough to say something. The blended multiples midpoint of $79.76 against a $110.38 price says it is 28% expensive, and refusing to engage with that is refusing to do the job.
devils_advocate.what_would_prove_it: Whether the multiples table's rows are independent measurements of the same company or one measurement repeated, and whether the trailing window they are computed over describes the business that exists today.
devils_advocate.already_visible: Yes, and it defeats the counter on the arithmetic. The three rows are ev_sales ($106.48 at cohort median), ev_gross_profit ($109.24) and p_tbv ($23.55) against a $110.38 price. Two of them say the stock is worth almost exactly what it trades at; the third says it is worth a fifth of that, and it is the third that drags the blend to $79.76. p_tbv of 19.7x on a company whose entire tangible equity is $186 million is not a valuation, it is a division — iRhythm's productive asset is an FDA-cleared algorithm and a payor-contract network, neither of which has a book value. That is the RIOT/EPRT refusal test firing (rows straddling the price, cohort 'not ranked'), and the MXL test firing too: quarterly revenue is inflecting, so the trailing window every row divides by describes a company roughly 15% smaller than the one trading today. Discard p_tbv and the remaining two say 'fair', which is not a thesis either. On the DCF side there is genuinely nothing: cfo less capex over the window is [$34.5M, -$30.6M, -$90.5M], H1 2026 free cash flow was $4.4 million, and `nonpositive_normalized_fcff` is correct.
devils_advocate.unresolved: The reimbursement question, which is the whole stock. I could not find a dated 2026 rate action explaining the 13.8% one-month decline — the company news in the store is uniformly positive about Q2 and the analyst commentary repeats 'reimbursement pressures remain' without citing an event. So I record that I do not know what the market is discounting, and that not knowing is the reason I would not underwrite this either way. I also could not size the cybersecurity liability: the company says it is 'not reasonably likely to have a material impact' and holds insurance, but HIPAA breach notification, OCR enforcement and class actions on a PHI exfiltration are not usually free and none of it is quantified anywhere.

what_changed: Three things, two of them absent from the engine entirely. (1) OPERATING INFLECTION: Q2 2026 revenue $224.2 million (+20.1%), gross margin 72.8% (+160bp), net loss $0.4 million against $14.2 million, adjusted EBITDA $43.3 million (19.3% margin), unrestricted cash and marketable securities $591.3 million. FY2026 guidance RAISED to $880-890 million of revenue and 13.0-14.0% adjusted EBITDA margin. FDA clearance of a third-generation algorithm expected to cut clinician review time ~50% and save ~$100 million cumulatively over five years. (2) A MATERIAL CYBERSECURITY INCIDENT, filed under Item 1.05 on 2026-06-15: unauthorised activity identified 2026-06-08 on third-party-hosted business applications; on 2026-06-09 a threat actor claimed to hold proprietary data, PATIENT PROTECTED HEALTH INFORMATION and other personal information and demanded payment; the company confirmed data was exfiltrated and determined the incident material on 2026-06-10 'in light of the volume of the potentially affected data'. Clinical and device systems were not involved. (3) The VitalConnect acquisition, signed 2026-08-05 for cash AND unregistered stock, cleared HSR on 2026-09-18 and is expected to close in early October 2026.
consensus_case: At $110.38 iRhythm is a $3.6 billion market capitalisation and roughly $3.7 billion enterprise value on 2026 guided revenue of $880-890 million and a guided adjusted EBITDA margin of 13.0-14.0% — about 4.2x forward sales and 31x forward adjusted EBITDA. The market is paying a growth multiple for a company that has just crossed into profitability: Q2 revenue rose 20.1% to $224.2 million, gross margin reached 72.8%, the net loss narrowed to $0.4 million, and adjusted EBITDA margin improved 1,090 basis points to 19.3%. Against that, the stock is down 37.4% over twelve months and 13.8% in the last month, which says the market is discounting something the income statement does not show — a single-product franchise (Zio long-term continuous ECG) whose price is set administratively by Medicare contractors and commercial payors, a material cybersecurity breach involving patient protected health information, and an acquisition closing in October. Nobody at this price is arguing the business is broken; they are arguing about what the reimbursement rate will be.
base_case_rationale: I am not supplying one. There is no cash-flow base to apply a growth rate to and no defensible substitute. See below.
key_risks: A single product family whose price is set administratively by Medicare contractors and followed by commercial payors — the most cited risk on the name and the one I could not resolve
Material cybersecurity incident (Item 1.05, June 2026) with confirmed exfiltration of patient protected health information and an extortion demand; liability unquantified anywhere in the filings
VitalConnect closes early October 2026 partly in unregistered stock, so the share count and the balance sheet both change immediately after this brief
Free cash flow is only just positive — $4.4 million in H1 2026 — on $46 million a year of capitalised Zio device spend; the inflection is real but thin
Stock is down 37.4% over twelve months against a rising sector, and I could not identify the dated cause
watch_for: Any CMS or MAC rate action on the long-term continuous ECG codes — the single fact that decides this equity
Q3 2026 free cash flow: whether the $37.5 million Q2 figure is a run rate or a seasonal peak
The VitalConnect closing: share count issued, purchase price allocation, and what it does to the adjusted EBITDA margin guide
Any disclosure quantifying the cybersecurity incident — notification costs, OCR action, or litigation
